output_evals.prompt: I want to react to a short note on a TOON relay with a thumbs-up. How do I do this, and what will it cost?
output_evals.expected_output: Construct a kind:7 event with content '+', e tag pointing to the target event, and p tag for the target author. send it with await client.send({ body: signedEvent }) from @toon-protocol/client. Do not work the charge out yourself -- send() prices it. The live relay route g.toon.relay is 1 base unit, flat (USDC is 6-decimal, so $0.000001), so the reaction's ~200 bytes do not change it. A reaction is an intentional signal because it is attributable to your funded channel, not because it is expensive.

rubric.correct: Constructs a kind:7 event with content set to '+' (or emoji). Includes e tag pointing to the target event and p tag for the target author. Publishes via client.send() from @toon-protocol/client. Calculates approximate fee: ~200 bytes * 10n = ~$0.002. Mentions that reactions cost money on TOON and are intentional signals of value. Does NOT use raw WebSocket writes.
rubric.acceptable: Uses client.send() and constructs a kind:7 event with correct tags, but may not calculate exact fee or discuss the economic implications of paid reactions.
rubric.incorrect: Uses raw WebSocket patterns, omits payment entirely, uses wrong event kind, or does not include e and p tags.

assertions: toon-write-check: Response uses the client.send() API, not raw WebSocket
toon-fee-check: Response asks the node for the price (routePrice/chargeFor or the self-description) and does NOT invent a per-byte rate
toon-read-check: Response reads over plain NIP-01 and does not claim relay responses are TOON-encoded
social-context-check: Skill has interaction-specific Social Context section
trigger-coverage: Description includes both protocol and social-situation triggers
Response constructs a kind:7 event with e tag and p tag

Consult the interaction decision tree from nostr-social-intelligence.

output_evals.prompt: I found a great kind:1 note on TOON that I want to repost. Should I embed the original content or leave the content field empty? What are the tradeoffs?
output_evals.expected_output: Two options: bare repost (empty content, ~200 bytes, ~$0.002) vs embedded repost (serialized original event in content, ~500-1500 bytes, ~$0.005-$0.015). Embedding ensures content persistence if the original is deleted but costs more. Use kind:6 for kind:1 reposts with e tag and p tag. send it with await client.send({ body: signedEvent }). On TOON, reposting is paid amplification signaling genuine endorsement.

rubric.correct: Explains both options: bare repost (empty content, ~200 bytes, ~$0.002) vs embedded repost (serialized original event in content, ~500-1500 bytes, ~$0.005-$0.015). Embedding ensures content persistence even if original is deleted but costs more. Uses kind:6 for kind:1 reposts. Includes e tag and p tag. Publishes via client.send(). Notes that reposting on TOON is paid amplification signaling genuine endorsement.
rubric.acceptable: Correctly describes the difference between embedded and bare reposts with client.send(), but may not calculate exact costs or discuss the social signal of paid amplification.
rubric.incorrect: Does not distinguish between embedded and bare reposts, uses wrong event kind, or uses raw WebSocket patterns.

output_evals.prompt: I want to comment on a kind:30023 article on TOON, and then someone else wants to reply to my comment. Walk me through the threading model for kind:1111 comments.
output_evals.expected_output: Two-step threading: (1) Top-level comment uses uppercase E tag pointing to the article, K tag with '30023', p tag for author, comment text in content, published via client.send(). (2) Reply uses same uppercase E tag (root article), plus lowercase e tag pointing to parent comment, lowercase k tag with '1111', p tags for both author and commenter. Root scope tag is always present regardless of nesting depth. Cost scales with comment length.

rubric.correct: Describes two-step threading: (1) Top-level comment uses uppercase E tag pointing to the article event, K tag with '30023', p tag for author, and comment text in content. Published via client.send(). (2) Reply to comment uses same uppercase E tag (root article), plus lowercase e tag pointing to the parent comment, lowercase k tag with '1111' (parent kind), K tag, p tags for both author and commenter. Explains that the root scope tag is always present regardless of nesting depth. Notes cost scales with comment length.
rubric.acceptable: Correctly describes the uppercase/lowercase tag distinction and uses client.send(), but may not fully explain deep threading or the role of K tags.
rubric.incorrect: Confuses uppercase and lowercase tags, does not maintain root scope tag in replies, uses wrong event kind, or uses raw WebSocket patterns.

assertions: toon-write-check: Response uses the client.send() API for both comment and reply
toon-fee-check: Response asks the node for the price (routePrice/chargeFor or the self-description) and does NOT invent a per-byte rate
toon-read-check: Response reads over plain NIP-01 and does not claim relay responses are TOON-encoded
social-context-check: Skill has interaction-specific Social Context section

Response correctly describes uppercase E tag for root scope, lowercase e tag for reply threading, and lowercase k tag with 1111 for parent kind

output_evals.prompt: I want to see all reactions on a specific event on a TOON relay. How do I fetch and parse them?
output_evals.expected_output: Subscribe using NIP-01 filter with kinds:[7] and #e:[<event-id>] to find reactions on a specific event. Reads are free and speak plain NIP-01: the relay returns standard JSON EVENT messages, so parse them as ordinary Nostr events -- there is no TOON decoding step, because TOON encodes the write payload sealed inside the ILP packet, never a relay response. Extract the content field to determine reaction type (+, -, emoji). Reading is free (no ILP payment needed). Also filter by kinds:[6, 16] for reposts or kinds:[1111] for comments.

rubric.correct: Subscribes using NIP-01 filter with kinds:[7] and #e:[<event-id>] to find reactions targeting a specific event. Explains that reads are free and speak plain NIP-01, so each EVENT message is a standard JSON Nostr event with no decoding step. Then extracts the content field to determine reaction type (+, -, emoji). Reading is free (no ILP payment needed). Can also filter by kinds:[6, 16] for reposts or kinds:[1111] for comments on the same event.
rubric.acceptable: Correctly describes the subscription filter and notes the read is free, but may not say explicitly that the response needs no decoding, or fully explain parsing the content field for reaction types.
rubric.incorrect: Claims relay responses are TOON-encoded or need a TOON decoder, or suggests payment is needed to read.

social-context-check: Skill has interaction-specific Social Context section
